name: Painleve-Gullstrand / Lemaitre slicing of Schwarzschild: sqrt(2m/R) is the marginally bound free-fall velocity (Newtonian escape velocity)

published_statement: Martel-Poisson (gr-qc/0001069) Sec. II: for ingoing radial timelike geodesics of Schwarzschild, tdot = E~/f, rdot^2 + f = E~^2 (2.1), E~ = 1/sqrt(1 - v_inf^2) (2.2); 'we specialize to ... E~ = 1; our observers are all starting at infinity with a zero initial velocity', so rdot = -sqrt(1-f) = -sqrt(2M/r); u_a = -d_a T with T = t + int sqrt(1-f)/f dr (2.3)-(2.5), giving ds^2 = -dT^2 + (dr + sqrt(2M/r) dT)^2 + r^2 dOmega^2 (2.7); 'the surfaces T = constant are intrinsically flat'. Hamilton-Lisle (gr-qc/0411060) eq.(1)-(2): 'beta is the Newtonian escape velocity ... beta = (2GM/r)^(1/2) and t_ff is the proper time experienced by an object that free falls radially inward from zero velocity at infinity'; 'Inside the horizon, the infall velocity exceeds the speed of light'. Lemaitre chart (de Haro 2601.18660 eqs 18, 28-29): E = 0 (Newtonian-energy convention) trajectories rdot = -sqrt(2MG/r), R - T = (2/3) r^(3/2)/sqrt(2MG), ds^2 = dT^2 - (2MG/r) dR^2, T = the free-fall proper time (the same function as PG time, de Haro eq.26 first line = MP eq.2.5).
published_hypotheses: Schwarzschild vacuum, M > 0 (Martel-Poisson eq 1.1; Faraoni-Vachon Sec.4: PG observers do not exist where the Misner-Sharp-Hernandez mass is negative -- negative-mass Schwarzschild, AdS, RN inside r = Q^2/2M)
radial, timelike, freely falling (geodesic) observers (MP Sec. II)
E~ = 1: start at infinity with zero initial velocity -- marginally bound (MP eq 2.2, p = 1)
ingoing branch rdot < 0: covers exterior + black-hole region, not the white-hole region; time reverse gives the outgoing chart (MP Sec. II, Fig.1)
hypersurface orthogonality of the congruence, automatic for radial motion (MP Sec. V: u_a = -mu d_a T, mu = const iff also geodesic)

static spherical generalization (MP Sec. IV, eq 4.1): slices flat 'Unless psi = 0 and p = 1, these surfaces are not intrinsically flat'; Hamilton-Lisle eq (3)-(4) beta = sqrt(2M(r)/r) with Misner-Sharp M(r) for metrics with g_tt g_rr = -1
dynamic generalization (Nielsen-Visser via Faraoni-Vachon eqs 4.1-4.6): shift v = c(t,R) sqrt(2M_MSH/R), c = e^{-Phi}/(dt_bar/dt) -- a lapse factor multiplies sqrt(2m/R); breaks down where M_MSH < 0

'Newtonian escape velocity' / relative-speed reading requires a static observer, i.e. r > 2M (Hamilton-Lisle: beta = 1 at the horizon, > 1 inside; objects cannot move faster than light through the river)
hypothesis_drift: driven.py:212-213 'The Gamma = 1 surface IS the PG foliation' is stated without 'in Schwarzschild vacuum'. Re-derived F1: Gamma = W = 1 <=> intrinsically flat slicing holds in ANY spherical spacetime, so the flat-slice ('generalised PG') reading survives in general; the source's PG = geodesic observers from rest at infinity (MP Sec. II) needs vacuum Schwarzschild (or psi = 0 and d_r N = 0, F2). WEAKENED in wording; on the witness the tree actually uses (Schwarzschild) it is exact.

driven.py:390-392 (threshold_speed docstring 'the Painleve-Gullstrand shift and the local escape velocity') and drivensource.py:175-176 ('sqrt(2m/R) is the Painleve-Gullstrand shift') apply to general m (Misner-Sharp) and general slicing. DROPPED hypothesis: unit lapse. Published generalization (Faraoni-Vachon eq 4.6; MP Sec. IV psi = 0; Hamilton-Lisle g_tt g_rr = -1) and re-derivation F1: ADM shift = N sqrt(2m/R); only the normal observers' areal velocity U_n = -beta/N equals sqrt(2m/R) for every N. 'Local escape velocity' further needs a static observer (r > 2m, G2) and a conserved Killing energy, which a non-static spacetime lacks.

driven.py:205-206 and drivensource.py:180-181 'areal velocity of MARGINALLY BOUND radial free fall -- free fall from rest at infinity': in non-vacuum the Gamma = 1 observers are geodesic only if d_r N = 0 (F2, e.g. LTB dust with E(rho) = 0); with pressure they are accelerated and 'from rest at infinity' has no conserved-energy meaning. 'Marginally bound' survives as the Misner-Sharp/LTB definition Gamma^2 - 1 = 2E = 0. WEAKENED in general; exact in Schwarzschild (G1, G3) and dust.

No drift, recorded as agreement: m < 0. Faraoni-Vachon show PG observers cannot exist where M_MSH < 0; the tree already returns None from threshold_speed for m < 0 (driven.py:392-395) and makes no PG claim there.

No drift, recorded as agreement: drivensource.py:188-189, 373-374 'Lemaitre (= PG) slicing ... PG brought to the diagonal form'. Re-derived L3: substituting d rho = d tau + sqrt(R/r_s) dR turns the Lemaitre metric into MP eq (2.7) exactly, so Lemaitre time IS PG time (same foliation); the charts differ only in spatial threading (comoving rho vs areal r). The identification is a statement about slicing and is exact.

No drift: E3 at drivensource.py:435-439 carries W > 0 in its hypotheses; Z2 shows it is load-bearing (drop it and W = -1, U = 0, m = 0 is a counterexample). driven.py:203 states 'Gamma = 1 <=> U^2 = 2m/R' without the sign but defines Gamma as a positive sqrt (driven.py:376-381), so the hypothesis is carried.

Guard against over-reading, not a drift: driven.py:217-220 'U IS NOT CAPPED AT 1'. True (N1: |U| = sqrt(r_s/R) > 1 iff R < r_s) and matches Hamilton-Lisle ('inside the horizon the infall velocity exceeds the speed of light'); U = dR/dtau is a coordinate rate with no static observer inside r_s, so it is not a local relative speed above c. The tree claims only that no light-speed cap on U exists, which is what holds.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: the result is a closed-form statement about the exact Schwarzschild solution, so no measured datum enters it and none that came later can move it (data_at_publication: none). What the 1921-22 authors lacked was interpretation, not data. As Hamilton-Lisle (gr-qc/0411060 p.1) report it, Painlevé took the flat spatial metric to mean that redshift predictions drawn from ds^2 were 'pure imagination', while Gullstrand saw that observables do not depend on the chart. Lemaitre 1933 then showed r = r_s to be a coordinate singularity. That error was repaired inside the theory by 1933 without new data, and the tree uses the repaired form. Later work adds scope, not correction: negative Misner-Sharp mass (Faraoni-Vachon 2020), lapse != 1 and pressure (Nielsen-Visser as restated there; Martel-Poisson Sec. IV). Evidence either way: every step was re-derived here symbolically (15/15 PASS). M's hypothesis does not bite on this result.
grade_evidence: As the canonical entry scopes it (Schwarzschild vacuum, Lemaitre = PG foliation, marginally bound radial free fall), every statement was re-derived independently, and none depends on a datum. Specifically: the Lemaitre metric is vacuum (L1). Its W = 1, U = -sqrt(r_s/R) and m = r_s/2 (L2). Lemaitre time is PG time (L3). The E = 1 geodesic has rdot = -sqrt(2M/r), and that is its speed relative to static observers outside r_s (G1, G2). Gamma equals the Killing energy per unit mass, so Gamma = 1 means marginally bound (G3). |U| > 1 holds exactly for R < r_s (N1). The tree's z3 obligation E3 re-proves, and its W > 0 hypothesis is load-bearing and carried (Z1, Z2). The five rests_on_it flags all hold: THRESHOLD_IS_PAINLEVE_GULLSTRAND, PG_IS_COINCIDENCE_OF_NOTATION = False, AREAL_VELOCITY_IS_CAPPED_AT_LIGHTSPEED = False, and WAVECORRIDOR_PG / 'PG is the W = 1 surface' (by F1 this even holds in general as the flat-slice statement). The drift is in the glosses the owners attach to the general threshold, and it is recorded as drift, not as grounds for downgrading, because no flag or refusal depends on it: 'the PG shift' needs unit lapse (F1), 'free fall / local escape velocity' needs geodesic normals and a static observer (F2, G2). Over-representation checked both ways. The tree's stronger wording is not endorsed beyond Schwarzschild or dust, and nothing is quoted as an error.
what_would_change_the_grade: It would become NARROWED if a downstream use in the tree relied on (a) sqrt(2m/R) being the ADM shift in a spacetime with lapse N != 1, or (b) the free-fall / escape-velocity / Killing-energy reading in a non-vacuum, non-dust or non-static region (e.g. a refusal argued from 'marginally bound free fall' with pressure). It would become WRONG only if a counterexample appeared to L1-L5 or G1-G3, and none is possible since these are exact symbolic identities. It would become OPEN if the original 1921-1933 papers stated something materially different from the restatements. They were not read here (NAMED-NOT-READ), and four independent restatements agree.
